key_insight: Generative AI can produce multiple plausible turbulent flows, but physical fidelity requires validation beyond visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectra.
engineering_relevance: Potential uses include stochastic closures, flow super-resolution, data assimilation, and uncertainty quantification when observations or resolved scales are incomplete.
method: Reviews diffusion, score-based, and probability-transport methods for turbulence.
Examines probabilistic reconstruction, flow ensembles, reduced-order modeling, and temporal evolution.
Proposes physics-aware validation and an open, standardized benchmark ecosystem.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports no quantitative benchmark results; it advocates evaluating energy transfer, intermittency, conservation, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity, and generalization.
watch_item: Physically plausible-looking outputs may still miss extreme events or multiscale dynamics, making rigorous validation essential before engineering deployment.
paper_title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
